facts.statement: Invictibellatrix means "unconquered woman warrior" in Latin and is known from a single braincase from the Early Cretaceous Barremian Wessex Formation of England.
facts.quote: Invictibellatrix (Latin: "unconquered woman warrior") is an extinct genus of megaraptoran theropod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian age) Wessex Formation of England. The genus contains a single species, Invictibellatrix amberina, known from a single braincase.

facts.statement: The holotype braincase (NHMUK PV R 6775) was found on the Isle of Wight and was purchased by the Natural History Museum in London in May 1924.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the Natural History Museum in London, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen NHMUK PV R 6775. It was sold to the museum in May 1924 by the widow of the collector Reginald Walter Hooley.

facts.statement: Invictibellatrix was formally described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Cassius Morrison and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2026, Cassius Morrison and colleagues described Invictibellatrix amberina as a new genus and species of megaraptoran theropod

facts.statement: Invictibellatrix is estimated to have weighed between 200 and 300 kilograms and measured about 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Invictibellatrix is estimated to have a body mass between 200–300 kg and a body length of around 4 m.

facts.statement: It possesses three unique skull features, including a small recessus basipterygoideus on each side of the parabasisphenoíd, a lightly transversely compressed hourglass‑shaped crest, and curved depressions along the crest midline.
facts.quote: Three autapomorphies (unique derived traits) were recognized. On each side of the parabasisphenoíd in front of the recessus tympanicus anterior, a small recessus basipterygoideus is present. The crest on the back of the skull is lightly transversely compressed and has an hourglass profile. On the crest, distinctive, lightly curved depressions are present on the midline.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses generally place Invictibellatrix as a derived member of Megaraptoridae, a group otherwise known mainly from Late Cretaceous Gondwana.
facts.quote: These generally recovered Invictibellatrix as a derived member of the megaraptoran family Megaraptoridae, which is otherwise almost entirely restricted to the Late Cretaceous of Gondwana.

facts.statement: Invictibellatrix lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The only known fossil occurrence of Invictibellatrix is a single braincase from the Wessex Formation.
Neurocranial characters such as a sub‑circular occipital condyle, sub‑oval foramen magnum, and a sagittal nuchal crest support its assignment to Megaraptora.
The absence of megaraptorans in Late Cretaceous Laurasia is interpreted as a regional extinction rather than a true absence.
